# A Two-Continua Model of Sleep Health: Smoke-Test Excerpt

## Summary

Meng et al. [1] provide the first systematic review directly comparing the two leading multidimensional sleep health instruments, the Ru-SATED scale and the Sleep Health Index (SHI). The Buysse SATED paper [2] defined sleep health as "a multidimensional pattern of sleep-wakefulness, adapted to individual, social, and environmental demands, that promotes physical and mental well-being" [2, p. 12]. Knutson et al.'s National Sleep Foundation Sleep Health Index [3] relied on expert consensus and psychometric testing in nationally representative samples to operationalize the dimensions of the SHI as a questionnaire.

## References

[1] Meng, R., BaHammam, A.S., Dzierzewski, J.M., et al. (2026). Ru-SATED scale and Sleep Health Index: A systematic review of two leading multidimensional sleep health measures and frameworks across the globe. *Sleep Medicine Reviews*, 88, 102296. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smrv.2026.102296

[2] Buysse, D.J. (2014). Sleep health: Can we define it? Does it matter? *Sleep*, 37(1), 9–17. https://doi.org/10.5665/sleep.3298

[3] Knutson, K.L., Phelan, J., Paskow, M.J., Roach, A., Whiton, K., Langer, G., Hillygus, D.S., Mokrzycki, M., Broughton, W.A., Chokroverty, S., Lichstein, K.L., Weaver, T.E., & Hirshkowitz, M. (2017). The National Sleep Foundation's Sleep Health Index. *Sleep Health*, 3(4), 234–240. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.sleh.2017.05.011
